source_excerpts.text:
**I constructed a way to turn cancellation of an unknown memory field into a guarantee for an entire adaptive experiment, using one output bit per physical interrogation.**

The central move is to change what the instrument reports. A real-valued observation can have the correct mean while still carrying harmful dependence on hidden memory. For a binary observation, its mean determines its entire distribution. With a fresh private sign and a randomized comparator threshold, that distinction becomes useful: within a specified range, the returned bit has exactly the distribution it would have on a fresh specimen.

I then bounded the effect of excursions outside that range and combined the bound with the passive-energy argument. The resulting guarantee applies to adaptive query choices, stopping rules and subsequent tasks using the same specimen.

There is a complete finite example with a nontrivial certificate: **15 active probes, a finite 4,096-setting threshold generator, zero resets, and a certified failure probability below 5%.** Its expected duration is about **2,018 physical windows**. A direct ordinary alternative achieves its own certificate below 5% using **185 consecutive probes**. Thus the general construction spends calendar time to obtain a reusable statistical interface with fewer active probes; it has not established a speed advantage.

These are **new working results derived and checked in this P1 role**, without independent review or established priority.

The earlier record remains intact. The common-null and finite-correction constructions retain their original assumptions. The previous bounded-ADC execution still failed its zero-call comparison: its certified radii of \(1.83315\) and \(0.79078\) remain worse than \(0.282843\). The separate full-signed-read simulation remains a result under its stronger readout contract. I used your handoff and retrieved summaries; I have not read the unavailable original proof attachments.

> **Can one persistent specimen supply a reusable experimental interface whose complete observable behavior approximates a fresh-specimen interface, without identifying or resetting its hidden state?**
